definition: Planner (often seen in publications as "PLANNER" although it is not an acronym) is a programming language designed by Carl Hewitt at MIT, and first published in 1969.
details: First, subsets such as Micro-Planner and Pico-Planner were implemented, and then essentially the whole language was implemented as Popler by Julian Davies at the University of Edinburgh in the POP-2 programming language. Derivations such as QA4, Conniver, QLISP and Ether (see scientific community metaphor) were important tools in artificial intelligence research in the 1970s, which influenced commercial developments such as Knowledge Engineering Environment (KEE) and Automated Reasoning Tool (ART).

explainer.lead: Planner is a programming language designed by Carl Hewitt at MIT, first published in 1969. Its derivations were important AI research tools in the 1970s and influenced commercial systems.

tiers.eli5: It is an early computer language built for AI programs that reason, and later versions shaped the tools researchers used.
tiers.practitioner: Subsets like Micro-Planner and Pico-Planner were implemented first; Julian Davies implemented essentially the whole language as Popler in POP-2 at the University of Edinburgh.
tiers.paperLevel: Planner is a language rather than a formal metric; its derivations include QA4, Conniver, QLISP and Ether, which influenced commercial developments such as KEE and ART.

explainer.example: Popler, written in POP-2 at Edinburgh, implemented essentially the whole of the Planner language.
